messages:
Ana P: Quick async question before I merge the embeddings API change — want to lock on the contract for out-of-range inputs and batch overflow behavior.
Mike L: Which change is this? link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/789
Ana P: PR updates handling when an item exceeds token/char limit. Proposal summary: truncate input at token_limit, compute embedding, return embeddings in same order and same length as inputs, and surface a compact diagnostics field with per-item flags. Example:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{ "model": "rw-embed-1", "inputs": ["short", "<very long...>", ""] }

200 OK
{
  "data": [ [0.01, ...], [0.12, ...], [0.0, ...] ],
  "meta": { "diagnostics": [{"index":1,"truncated":true}], "batch_size":3 }
}
```
Sasha K: I like preserving order/length. Two concerns: (1) adding per-item flags to top-level response may be safer as optional `meta.diagnostics` (so older clients ignore it), (2) empty string -> do we return a zero-vector or a small learned embed? we should be explicit.
David R: Backwards-compat is key: `data` must stay a list of vectors aligned with input indexes. Do not introduce required schema changes. Optional `meta` is fine. For empty-string, prefer deterministic zero-vector for now (clear semantics) — we can change later with a major bump.
Ana P: Agreed — keep `data` shape identical and required. `meta.diagnostics` optional. For empty inputs we return zero-vector and document it. Also thinking about batch limits: what should we do if a client submits 100k items or hits payload-size > 50MB?
Mike L: We already have soft limits: per-request item cap 10k and 50MB payload. If exceeded we should 413 with a clear error and suggested retry strategy (split into N-sized chunks). Avoid partial success by default.
Sasha K: Can we support partial success mode as opt-in? `?mode=partial` or header `X-Embeddings-Mode: partial`. If opted-in, return 207 Multi-Status and `errors` list mapping failed indexes. That avoids surprising older clients.
David R: Implementing partial inflates complexity in runtime; opt-in header is reasonable but let's postpone unless a customer needs it. For now 413 + docs, and make sure SDKs handle chunking.
Ana P: Sounds good. I'll keep partial as future opt-in note. One more: do we include a `truncated_until` token index or just boolean? my vote: boolean and the truncated prefix length if we need to introspect.
Mike L: boolean plus `truncated_tokens` (count) is fine in diagnostics. Keep that off the hot path (meta).
Ana P: @Mike L @Sasha K quick review request on the serializer + docs in the PR — pinging codeowners. Also adding tests for zero-vector and oversized payload. cc @David R
Mike L: I'll take serializer changes tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy-bot deployed branch pr-789 to dev-cluster in 2m — smoke tests queued.
Sasha K: small note for docs: add explicit example showing input null vs empty string vs missing item behavior. Some clients send nulls.
Ana P: Good call — spec: null -> 400 with message "null input not allowed; use empty string if intent is 'no content'". I'll add that.
David R: OK. If no objections I'll merge once CI and Mike's serializer review is in.
Ana P: Thanks all — updating PR with: keep required `data` list, optional `meta.diagnostics` with `index`, `truncated` boolean, optional `truncated_tokens` int, zero-vector for empty string, 413 for payload/size limits, nulls -> 400. Will ping again when ready.
